clock.help: Technical help, not legal advice. The window is 14 days (or your longer period) from delivery and runs to Monday when it ends on a weekend; public holidays can extend it too. The refund is due 14 days after the withdrawal arrived; for goods you may wait until they are back (status Return arrived) or the customer shows proof of sending, whichever comes first, unless you offered to collect them (Art. 13(3)). For services, the window counts from the order, and with the early start request the customer pays for the part provided.

Technical help, not legal advice.

proof.title: Proof log
proof.intro: A dated record of what your shop showed and which withdrawals it received, kept in your shop's own database. Each entry is chained to the one before by a SHA-256 hash, so a changed or deleted entry shows up when you check the chain. It holds no customer names, email addresses or order numbers. A snapshot is recorded once a day.
proof.unavailable: The proof log table is missing. Update or reinstall the plugin.
proof.loadFailed: The proof log could not be loaded.
proof.none: No entries yet. The first snapshot is recorded within a day, or press "Record a snapshot now".

proof.retentionAll: All entries are kept (plugin settings, Proof log).
proof.verifyBroken: Chain broken at entry {id}, after {count} intact entries. An entry was changed or deleted.

returns.title: Returns tool
returns.intro: Shopproof can send each new withdrawal to your returns tool or automation as signed JSON, and add a link to your returns portal to the customer's receipt. Set the addresses in the Shopproof settings (Returns tool card).
returns.on: On: each new withdrawal is sent to your returns tool.
returns.off: Off: no webhook address is set.
returns.secretHelp: Paste this into your returns tool. Each request carries the header X-Shopproof-Signature: t=<time>,v1=<signature>. The signature is the HMAC-SHA256, in hex, of the time, a dot and the request body, keyed with this secret. Keep the secret private.
returns.renewed: New secret made. Paste it into your returns tool, since the old one no longer works.
returns.testOk: Your returns tool accepted the test (status {code}).
returns.testRefused: Your returns tool refused the test with status {code}. Check the address and the secret there.
returns.testUnreachable: Your returns tool could not be reached. Check the address.

delivery.retrying: Returns tool: not accepted {time} (status {code}). Shopproof will try again.
delivery.failed: Returns tool: gave up {time} (status {code}). Please create the return by hand.

notes.policyOnlineUnsure_off: Withdrawal policy: not checked whether your revocation page says customers can also withdraw online, because Shopproof cannot judge pages in this language. Check it yourself. The official sentence: "{detail}"

notes.providerButton_off: Withdrawal button: the {detail} plugin has a shop ID set for its own withdrawal button, and Shopware's withdrawal button is on too, so customers may see two. Keep one: Shopware's button (Settings > Basic information), which Shopproof completes, or the {detail} button.
notes.priorPrice_ok: Reduced prices show the lowest price of the 30 days before the reduction.
notes.priorPriceCapped_off: Reduced prices show the lowest price of the 30 days before the reduction for the first {detail} products on sale that Shopproof checked. Your shop has more products, which were not checked here.
notes.priorPriceOff_off: {detail} products have a list price (shown crossed out), but "Show the lowest price of the 30 days before a reduction" is off in the Shopproof settings. EU price rules ask you to show it.
notes.priorPriceMissing_off: These products have a list price, but Shopproof has less than 30 days of their prices, so no lowest price shows. Fill in Shopware's own "Cheapest price (last 30 days)" on the product (Prices): {detail}
notes.priorPriceHigher_off: These products cross out a list price that is higher than their 30-day lowest price, so the reduction looks bigger than it is. A percentage must be worked out from the 30-day lowest price (EU Court of Justice, C-330/23): {detail}

bulk.title: Safety details for many products at once
bulk.intro: Fill in the product safety details of many products in a spreadsheet, with Shopware's own Import/Export:
bulk.step1: Open Settings > Import/Export, tab Export, and export with the profile "Shopproof: product safety". Tick "Export product variants" if your variants have their own details.
bulk.step2: Fill in the columns in the file. Leave the product_number column as it is. Hazard pictograms keep the form of the export, for example ["GHS02","GHS07"].
bulk.step3: Import the file with the same profile, tab Import. Products are matched by product number, and an empty cell leaves the value as it is. A row with an unknown number is not imported: Shopware then reports the import as failed and offers a file with those rows, while the other rows are saved.
bulk.manufacturers: Most products take their details from their manufacturer. The profile "Shopproof: manufacturer safety details" works the same way for manufacturers, matched by the id column.
bulk.bulkEdit: To give a few products the same details, select them in Catalogues > Products, choose Bulk edit and fill in "Shopproof: product safety (GPSR)" under Custom fields.

placement.title: Check where the withdrawal link appears
placement.intro: Here you see your shop pages as shoppers see them, on a computer and on a phone. The withdrawal button has a blue frame, and anything that covers your theme's content has a red dashed frame. Click around your shop in the preview and each page is checked again. The check runs in your browser and nothing leaves your shop; only the number of pages that passed is saved.

nonEu.title: Selling into the EU from abroad
nonEu.intro: You told Shopproof that your business is established outside the EU and EEA. EU consumer rules apply to your sales to EU buyers in the same way as for EU shops, so the withdrawal button and the other features work as usual. On top of that, these duties apply to sellers from outside the EU.
nonEu.summary: Extra duties for sellers from abroad still to check: {open} of {total}.
nonEu.empty: Not checked: the rules list in this shop has no duties for sellers outside the EU yet. Use "Check for rule updates now" further down.

status.good: An EU responsible person is entered in the Shopproof settings and shown with your products.
status.bad: No EU responsible person entered yet. Enter the name and address in the Shopproof settings (Product safety), and Shopproof shows them with every product.
status.todo: Check yourself. Shopproof cannot see this from your shop.

nonEu.footer: Shopproof cannot act as your EU responsible person, IOSS intermediary or GDPR representative: you appoint them yourself. This is technical help, not legal or tax advice.
nonEu.guide: Guide for sellers outside the EU

recommended.intro: Shopproof read your products and storefronts. One press switches on these for all sales channels, each in the place shops usually show it. You can undo it, or change each one in the Shopproof settings.

guarantee.title: Legal guarantee notice
guarantee.where: On product pages, below the product description.
guarantee.why: EU law asks shops that sell goods to show it.

priorPrice.title: Lowest price before a sale
priorPrice.where: Next to reduced prices only. Products not on sale show nothing.
priorPrice.why: EU rules ask for the lowest price of the 30 days before a reduction.

deliveryLine.where: Above the Go to checkout button in the cart and at the top of the checkout page, read from your storefronts' countries and payment methods.
deliveryLine.why: Shoppers must see where you deliver and how they can pay before they order.

digital.title: Download consent at checkout

dispute.title: Dispute statement
dispute.tick: True for my shop: we have not agreed to and are not obliged to take part.
dispute.why: Most small shops answer this way. Shops in Germany with more than 10 employees must say whether they take part (§ 36 VSBG). If an arbitration board or a trade association rule binds you, choose in the Shopproof settings instead.

reviews.title: Review check notice
reviews.tick: True for my shop: our reviews are Shopware's own, and no other plugin or service checks them.
reviews.why: Shopware does not check whether a reviewer bought the product. Shops that show reviews must say whether they check them; saying they are checked when they are not is banned.

exclusionHints.title: Suggested withdrawal exclusions
exclusionHints.intro: The law lets shops exclude some goods from withdrawal. Shopproof found these in your shop. Nothing is excluded for you: tick only what fits and save. Excluded items still show on the withdrawal form with your explanation, and your copy of each withdrawal names them, so you can check each case.

why.download: Digital products, once the customer agreed that the download starts before the withdrawal period ends and confirmed that they lose the right to withdraw (Art. 16(m) of Directive 2011/83/EU). Your download consent boxes at checkout ask for both.
why.custom: The name suggests goods made to the customer's specifications or clearly personalised (Art. 16(c) of Directive 2011/83/EU). Exclude it only if every product in it is made that way.
why.hygiene: The name suggests sealed goods that cannot be returned for health or hygiene reasons once unsealed after delivery (Art. 16(e) of Directive 2011/83/EU). The exception covers only items whose seal was broken, so check each withdrawal.

exclusionHints.saved: Excluded {count} suggestion from withdrawal, for all sales channels. You can change it in the Shopproof settings. | Excluded {count} suggestions from withdrawal, for all sales channels. You can change them in the Shopproof settings.

exclusionHints.note: Saved for all sales channels; a sales channel with its own list keeps it. Whether an exception applies is your call. Technical help, not legal advice.

greenClaims.title: Green claims
greenClaims.intro: Since 27 September 2026, EU law bans generic environmental claims such as "eco-friendly", "climate friendly" or "sustainable" unless the product has recognised excellent environmental performance (for example the EU Ecolabel) or the same page says exactly what the claim means. Claims that a product is climate neutral or has a reduced climate impact because of offsetting are banned outright (Directive (EU) 2024/825). Shopproof looks for the Directive's own example words in your product names and descriptions (default language), in all 24 EU languages.
greenClaims.notChecked: Not checked: Shopproof could not read your products or its word lists just now. Reload the page in a minute.
greenClaims.noProducts: Not checked yet: the shop has no active products.
greenClaims.scopeSome: Checked your {checked} most recently changed products of {total}.
greenClaims.aside: {count} mention was left out because the sentence says the opposite, is about disposal, or gives the details (a percentage or an ecolabel). | {count} mentions were left out because the sentence says the opposite, is about disposal, or gives the details (a percentage or an ecolabel).
greenClaims.none: None uses the example words from the Directive.
greenClaims.limits: Shopproof only finds the Directive's example words and close forms of them. Other green claims, pictures and colours can still count as claims. Technical help, not legal advice.
greenClaims.worth: {count} product worth checking | {count} products worth checking
greenClaims.canBeFine: These words can be fine, for example with an EU Ecolabel for that claim, or when the same page says exactly what is meant ("100% of the cotton is organic"). Shopproof does not decide whether a claim is allowed: please check each one. Technical help, not legal advice.
greenClaims.more: And {count} more product. | And {count} more products.
greenClaims.genericText: words such as "eco-friendly", "umweltfreundlich" or "biodegradable". Allowed only with recognised excellent environmental performance for that claim (the EU Ecolabel, an officially recognised EN ISO 14024 label, or top performance under EU law, such as energy class A for "energy efficient"), or when the same page says exactly what is meant (UCPD Annex I point 4a).
greenClaims.broadText: words such as "sustainable" or "nachhaltig". They also cover social qualities, so even an ecolabel is not enough on its own (recital 10). Say exactly what is meant on the same page, or leave the word out.
greenClaims.offsettingText: words such as "climate neutral", "CO2 neutral" or "reduced climate impact". Banned when they rest on offsetting emissions, for example with carbon credits; allowed only when they rest on the product's own lifecycle (UCPD Annex I point 4c). Telling shoppers that you support climate projects stays allowed when it is not misleading.

a11y.title: Accessibility statement
a11y.intro: Since 28 June 2025, most shops that sell to consumers in the EU must make their shop accessible and publish an accessibility statement: what the shop does for accessibility, the barriers it knows of, how to report one and which authority to contact. Very small businesses (fewer than 10 people and no more than 2 million euros a year) are exempt for their services. Most shops link the statement in the footer, next to the legal notice and privacy policy.
a11y.linkCheck: The placement check above also shows, for each page, whether it links to accessibility information.
a11y.draftIntro: Fill in what you know. The draft below changes as you type; copy it into a shopping experience or CMS page, read it, change anything that does not fit and link it in your footer. Nothing is stored or sent. The draft never says your shop is fully accessible. It says what you work towards and what you did.
a11y.emailHelp: Where shoppers tell you about a barrier. It goes on the page.
a11y.aboutHelp: One sentence. Leave it empty for: browse products, choose options, put them in the cart and order.
a11y.measuresHelp: One item per line, for example: All product photos have a text description.
a11y.barriersHelp: One item per line, for example: The size guide is hard to use with a keyboard.
a11y.noAuthority: Shopproof knows the authority for Austria, Germany, France, Italy and the Netherlands. For another country the draft leaves a marked gap for you to fill in.
a11y.where: Technical help, not legal advice. Read the draft and change anything that does not fit your shop before you publish it.

marketplaces.title: Sell on eBay or Amazon
marketplaces.intro: eBay and Amazon ask for the same product safety details as your product pages. Shopproof fills them in from the product safety settings, your manufacturers and your products, matched by product number (eBay calls it Custom label, Amazon calls it SKU). Nothing is sent: you download the files and upload them yourself. Technical help, not legal advice.
marketplaces.ebayStep1: In eBay Seller Hub, open Reports, then Uploads. Choose "Get template", then Listings and "Edit price and quantity", and download the file.
marketplaces.ebayStep2: Choose that file here and click "Fill in safety details".
marketplaces.ebayStep3: Upload the file you get back on the same eBay page, then check eBay's results report.
marketplaces.ebayNote: eBay removes details that are sent blank, so listings Shopproof cannot fill completely are left out of the file. The file also holds your prices and stock as eBay had them, so upload it soon after downloading it.
marketplaces.amazonStep2: In Seller Central, enter each manufacturer and EU responsible person from the contacts file once. Amazon links listings to them by email address.
marketplaces.amazonStep3: Copy the columns of the listings file into Amazon's inventory file for your products and upload it as a partial update.
marketplaces.amazonNote: Amazon takes warnings and safety information as documents or pictures, not as text. Add them in Seller Central.

marketplaces.amazonFilled: {filled} of {total} active product is in the files. | {filled} of {total} active products are in the files.
marketplaces.failed: Not done: the shop could not make the file. Try again, and if it keeps failing, contact Shopproof support.

assistant.title: AI assistant
assistant.intro: Connect an AI assistant that supports MCP (for example Claude Desktop, Cursor or another MCP app) and let it set up Shopproof for you, or ask it about your withdrawals and proof log. The assistant talks to this shop directly; Shopproof does not see or keep what it reads. Technical help, not legal advice.
assistant.where: Whatever the assistant reads is sent to the AI service you use, under that service's terms. Changes are shown to you first, recorded in the proof log and can be undone below. The assistant never changes orders, customers or withdrawals, never sends emails and never deletes anything.
